column1: # DARS contact-energy matrix, 18 ACP atom types.
#   Table I ("Contact Energies of the DARS Potential") of:
#     Kozakov D., Brenke R., Comeau S.R., Vajda S.
#     "PIPER: An FFT-Based Protein Docking Program with Pairwise Potentials"
#   Atom typing is the 18-type ACP scheme of
#     Zhang C., Vasmatzis G., Cornette J.L., DeLisi C., J Mol Biol 267:707-726, 1997.
#   DARS frequency counting used a 6.5 A contact cutoff (Methods, PDF p.20).
# TRANSCRIPTION STATUS: transcribed by hand from the PDF table.
#   Checked: (a) matrix is exactly symmetric, (b) 18 values per row,
#   (c) signs of the entries the paper calls out in prose agree --
#       RNh-RNh slightly attractive (-0.36), CSg-CSg large artifact (-5.67).
#   NOT yet checked against an independent electronic source.
# UNITS: the paper reports these as contact energies from eps_IJ = -RT ln(p_IJ),
#   i.e. in units of RT. They are used inside E_pair with weight w3
# NOTE: the paper's production scoring function uses the linear combination
#   The ACP matrix is NOT in this paper (see Zhang et al. 1997). Because the
#   combination is linear and both matrices are symmetric, JuPIPER should
#   eigendecompose the *combined* matrix once rather than each separately --
#   that keeps the correlation count at P, not 2P.
# FORMAT: tab-separated. First column = row atom type label. 18x18, row-major.
# Type order: N Ca C O GCa Cb KNz KCd DOd RNh NNd RNe SOg HNe YCz FCz LCd CSg
#   (Greek letters spelled out: z=zeta, d=delta, h=eta, e=epsilon, g=gamma, b=beta)
